To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed new reinforcement learning algorithms for average-payoff Markovian decision processes that are analogous to the TD and Q-learning reinforcement learning algorithms for discounted-payoff Markov decision processes.

the policy evaluation and policy improvement problems in average-payoff Markovian decision processes can be solved by the stochastic approximation methods that are analogous to the TD and Q-learning methods for discounted-payoff MDPs, and that the resulting average-payoff Q-learning method is a variation of the R-learning method.

(1) the average-payoff problem is more difficult than the discounted-payoff problem because the former has a more complex solution, but (2) the new algorithms are able to solve the average-payoff problems, and (3) the new algorithms perform as well as, or better than, the discounted-payoff algorithms in solving the average-payoff task.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the average-payoff RL problem, which we formulate as a Markovian decision process with average-payoff reward function.
developing RL algorithms for the average-payoff case.
reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms for average-payoff problems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the average-payoff case is much harder than the discounted case and that, in general, the average-payoff RL problem is a much harder problem than the discounted-payoff RL problem.
, in the case of a single agent, the average payoff RL problem is no more difficult to solve than the discounted payoff RL problem.
the average payoff RL algorithms are more efficient in terms of sample complexity, but the discount RL algorithms are more robust in the presence of noise.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have derived a new set of RL algorithms for average-payoff problems.

, for the average payoff case, we have developed new algorithms that have a better theoretical convergence rate than the R-learning algorithm and that are computationally simpler than the algorithms developed for the discounted payoff case.
the algorithms for the average-payoff case are very similar to those for the discounted-sum case, but that the average-payoff algorithms are somewhat simpler to understand and implement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the new algorithms are more robust than their discounted-payoff counterparts.
the average-payoff RL setting is a promising alternative for solving many RL tasks.
